name: Cervical Flexion
description: Cervical Flexion is a mild–moderate demand mobility / motor control exercise for the cervical spine region, targeting Deep cervical flexors, cervical extensors, sternocleidomastoid.
instructions: Set up in a stable, pain-free position appropriate for cervical spine. Perform Cervical Flexion with controlled tempo, maintaining neutral alignment and steady breathing. Stop the set if symptoms exceed 3/10 or form breaks down.
sets_reps: 2–3 sets × 10–12 reps, daily to every other day; pain ≤ 3/10
clinical_notes: Typical demand: Mild–Moderate. Progress only when the current dosage is completed with good control and no symptom flare for 24 h. Regress by reducing range, load or lever length.
load_dosage: 2–3 sets × 10–12 reps, daily to every other day; pain ≤ 3/10
tempo: 2 s concentric — 1 s hold — 3 s eccentric
breathing: Exhale on effort, inhale on return; avoid breath holding.
contraindications: Unhealed fracture or post-op precautions not yet cleared

instructions: Set up in a stable, pain-free position appropriate for balance & proprioception. Perform Catch-and-Throw Balance Training with controlled tempo, maintaining neutral alignment and steady breathing. Stop the set if symptoms exceed 3/10 or form breaks down.
sets_reps: 3 sets × 8–12 reps, 3–4× per week; 48 h between sessions
clinical_notes: Typical demand: Moderate–High. Progress only when the current dosage is completed with good control and no symptom flare for 24 h. Regress by reducing range, load or lever length.
load_dosage: 3 sets × 8–12 reps, 3–4× per week; 48 h between sessions
tempo: 2 s concentric — 1 s hold — 3 s eccentric
breathing: Exhale on effort, inhale on return; avoid breath holding.
contraindications: Unhealed fracture or post-op precautions not yet cleared

target_muscles: Primary and synergistic musculature relevant to the stated exercise
primary_muscles: Primary and synergistic musculature relevant to the stated exercise
instructions: Set up in a stable, pain-free position appropriate for neurorehabilitation. Perform Sit to Stand Practice with controlled tempo, maintaining neutral alignment and steady breathing. Stop the set if symptoms exceed 3/10 or form breaks down.
sets_reps: 3 sets × 8–12 reps, 3–4× per week; 48 h between sessions
clinical_notes: Typical demand: Moderate. Progress only when the current dosage is completed with good control and no symptom flare for 24 h. Regress by reducing range, load or lever length.
load_dosage: 3 sets × 8–12 reps, 3–4× per week; 48 h between sessions
tempo: 2 s concentric — 1 s hold — 3 s eccentric
breathing: Exhale on effort, inhale on return; avoid breath holding.
contraindications: Unhealed fracture or post-op precautions not yet cleared

tempo: 2 s concentric — 1 s hold — 3 s eccentric
breathing: Exhale on effort, inhale on return; avoid breath holding.
